5 Generation of Observer Time at the Dynamical-Description Stage

← Previous chapterChapter 4: Comparison-Stage Closure and Canonical Representation→ Next chapterChapter 6: Localization of Validity, Failure, and ApproximationContents

Take as input the exact operability

𝖤𝗑𝖺𝖼𝗍𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝖻𝗅𝖾⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{ExactOperable}\left[\mathsf{I}\right]

of Definition 4.175. For an observer-side information-coupling position and an object-specification index, the dynamical-description stage specifies the conditions that generate the ℭ\mathfrak{C}-derived observer-time quotient, the 𝔅\mathfrak{B}-derived object-state quotient, the ℭ⁢𝔇⁢𝔅\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}\mathfrak{B}-derived canonical trajectory relation, graph trajectories, and the family of canonical observable functions. In dependency order, these conditions provide the construction conditions for dynamical-description operability, law-description operability, differential-stage operability, and multi-object relations.

5.1 Generation of Dynamical Descriptions from the Canonical Comparison Quotient

Definition 5.1 (Dynamical-description quotient-role family).

Within the previously defined source-role family 𝖱𝗈𝗅src\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{src}}, define the family of roles that carry quotients at the dynamical-description stage by

𝖱𝗈𝗅dyn,quot:={ℭ,𝔅}\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{dyn\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak quot}}:=\{\mathfrak{C}% \mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\mathfrak{B}\}

Throughout this chapter, the compound superscript (dyn,σ)(\mathrm{dyn}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\sigma) on an object specific to the dynamical-description stage is abbreviated to σ\sigma only when the symbol root and σ\sigma uniquely determine that the object belongs to the dynamical-description stage; a lone (dyn)(\mathrm{dyn}) is omitted. To distinguish it from the source-side relation 𝖱𝖾𝗅src\mathsf{Rel}^{\mathrm{src}}, the complete form 𝖱𝖾𝗅dyn,src\mathsf{Rel}^{\mathrm{dyn\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak src}} is retained.

Definition 5.3 (Common evaluation rule for dynamical-description conditions).

The eight dynamical-description conditions below use the following common rule. For each condition, consider the subset of 𝖤𝗏𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼exact\mathsf{EvSpec}^{\mathrm{exact}} on which all predecessor conditions explicitly assumed in its definition hold. Denote this subset by DD, and let PP be the test stated in that definition on this domain. Define the condition KK, for every 𝖤𝗏∈𝖤𝗏𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼\mathsf{Ev}\in\mathsf{EvSpec}, by

K⁢(𝖤𝗏)⟺∃e∈D,𝖤𝗏=e∧P⁢(e).K(\mathsf{Ev})\Longleftrightarrow\exists e\in D\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak% \quad\mathsf{Ev}=e\ \wedge\ P(e).

The test formula in each individual definition is its expression on DD; outside DD, KK is false. This rule makes the conditions total without extending the domains on which their quotients or maps are constructed.

Proposition 5.4 (Foundational structure for dynamical description).

For a complete evaluation specification 𝖤𝗏∈𝖤𝗏𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼exact\mathsf{Ev}\in\mathsf{EvSpec}^{\mathrm{exact}}, the family of source-token sets

(𝖳𝗈𝗄R∗)R∈𝖱𝗈𝗅src\left(\mathsf{Tok}_{R}^{\ast}\right)_{R\in\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{src}}}

is determined, and the exact-operability object sequence

𝖤𝖮𝖲𝖾𝗊⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{EOSeq}[\mathsf{I}]

is generated.

Consequently, the canonical comparison quotient derived from ℭ⁢𝔇\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}, 𝖰𝗎cmp,can⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{Qu}^{\mathrm{cmp\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak can}}[\mathsf{I}], the exact operational time structure ℰop⁢[𝖨]\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{op}}[\mathsf{I}], the local order-coordinate structures

(𝖰𝗎R,uloc[𝖨],<R,uloc[𝖨],𝖯𝗋𝗃R,uloc[𝖨])(R,u)∈𝖱𝗈𝗅cmp×U\left(\mathsf{Qu}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{R\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak u}[\mathsf{I}% ]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak<_{R\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak u}^{\mathrm{% loc}}[\mathsf{I}]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Prj}_{R\mathchar 44% \relax\allowbreak u}^{\mathrm{loc}}[\mathsf{I}]\right)_{(R\mathchar 44\relax% \allowbreak u)\in\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{cmp}}\times U}

and the global order-coordinate structures

(𝖰𝗎Rord,can[𝖨],<Rord,can[𝖨],𝖯𝗋𝗃Rord,can[𝖨])R∈𝖱𝗈𝗅cmp\left(\mathsf{Qu}^{\mathrm{ord\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak can}}_{R}[\mathsf{% I}]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak<_{R}^{\mathrm{ord\mathchar 44\relax% \allowbreak can}}[\mathsf{I}]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Prj}_{R}^{% \mathrm{ord\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak can}}[\mathsf{I}]\right)_{R\in\mathsf% {Rol}^{\mathrm{cmp}}}

Proof.

By Definition 3.25, 𝒳=(ℐraw,𝖣𝖺𝗍src)\mathcal{X}=(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{raw}}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{% Dat}^{\mathrm{src}}). By Definition 3.24, (𝖳𝗈𝗄R∗)R∈𝖱𝗈𝗅src(\mathsf{Tok}_{R}^{\ast})_{R\in\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{src}}} is a component of 𝖣𝖺𝗍src\mathsf{Dat}^{\mathrm{src}}.

By Definition 4.175, under 𝖤𝗑𝖺𝖼𝗍𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝖻𝗅𝖾⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{ExactOperable}[\mathsf{I}], 𝖤𝖮𝖲𝖾𝗊⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{EOSeq}[\mathsf{I}] is generated. The structures listed in the proposition are recursive components of 𝖤𝖮𝖲𝖾𝗊⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{EOSeq}[\mathsf{I}]. ∎

𝖤𝗏∈𝖤𝗏𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼exact\mathsf{Ev}\in\mathsf{EvSpec}^{\mathrm{exact}}

Proposition 5.20 (Partial-order and generation properties of the canonical observer-time order).

Under

𝖤𝗑𝖺𝖼𝗍𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝖻𝗅𝖾⁢[𝖨],KGenTimeOrdAntiSym⁢(𝖤𝗏),\mathsf{ExactOperable}[\mathsf{I}]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad K_{% \mathrm{GenTimeOrdAntiSym}}(\mathsf{Ev})\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak

the relation ⪯ocan\preceq^{\mathrm{can}}_{o} is a partial order on 𝖰𝗎ℭ,ocan\mathsf{Qu}^{\mathrm{can}}_{\mathfrak{C}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak o}. The natural projection Θℭ,ocan\Theta^{\mathrm{can}}_{\mathfrak{C}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak o} preserves the source order. Moreover, ⪯ocan\preceq^{\mathrm{can}}_{o} is the least preorder on the canonical time quotient for which this natural projection preserves the source order.

Proof.

Paths of length zero give reflexivity of the generated preorder, and concatenation of finite paths gives transitivity. Antisymmetry is the condition KGenTimeOrdAntiSym⁢(𝖤𝗏)K_{\mathrm{GenTimeOrdAntiSym}}(\mathsf{Ev}). The canonical order is therefore a partial order.

If x⪯∗ℭyx\preceq_{\ast}^{\mathfrak{C}}y, the pair of natural-projection images belongs to 𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖮𝗋𝖽𝖤𝖽𝗀𝖾o\mathsf{TimeOrdEdge}_{o}. The resulting path of length one shows that the natural projection preserves order.

Take any preorder on the canonical time quotient for which the natural projection preserves the source order. Its relation contains 𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖮𝗋𝖽𝖤𝖽𝗀𝖾o\mathsf{TimeOrdEdge}_{o}. By reflexivity and transitivity, it also contains the reflexive transitive closure of that relation. This proves the stated minimality. ∎

Proposition 5.43 (Preorder property of the refinement relation).

The relation ⊑adm\sqsubseteq_{\mathrm{adm}} is a preorder on presentations of dynamical-description admissible quotients. Two mutually refining presentations are isomorphic under ≅adm\cong_{\mathrm{adm}}, and ⊑adm\sqsubseteq_{\mathrm{adm}} induces a partial order on the isomorphism classes.

Proof.

The family of identity maps satisfies every condition in Definition 5.42; hence reflexivity holds.

Suppose that

𝖠𝖽𝗆𝖰𝗎𝖯𝗋𝗌0⊑adm𝖠𝖽𝗆𝖰𝗎𝖯𝗋𝗌1⊑adm𝖠𝖽𝗆𝖰𝗎𝖯𝗋𝗌2\mathsf{AdmQuPrs}_{0}\sqsubseteq_{\mathrm{adm}}\mathsf{AdmQuPrs}_{1}% \sqsubseteq_{\mathrm{adm}}\mathsf{AdmQuPrs}_{2}

For each R∈𝖱𝗈𝗅quotR\in\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{quot}}, define

𝖱𝖾𝖿𝖬𝖺𝗉R,o;2→0:=𝖱𝖾𝖿𝖬𝖺𝗉R,o;1→0∘𝖱𝖾𝖿𝖬𝖺𝗉R,o;2→1\mathsf{RefMap}_{R\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak o;2\to 0}:=\mathsf{RefMap}_{R% \mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak o;1\to 0}\circ\mathsf{RefMap}_{R\mathchar 44% \relax\allowbreak o;2\to 1}

Surjectivity, factorization through the natural projection, equality of the images of the trajectory relations, and order preservation by the ℭ\mathfrak{C}-component are all preserved under composition; hence transitivity holds.

Suppose that two presentations mutually refine one another. For each R∈𝖱𝗈𝗅quotR\in\mathsf{Rol}^{\mathrm{quot}}, composing the two factorization identities shows that each of the two composites of the oppositely directed refinement maps agrees with the corresponding natural projection after precomposition by that projection. Since the natural projections are surjective, Lemma 4.181 implies that both composites are identity maps. The two families of maps are therefore mutually inverse families of bijections preserving the order and the trajectory relation. Thus mutual refinement gives an isomorphism, and antisymmetry holds on the isomorphism classes. ∎

Proposition 5.81 (Uniqueness of the generated time base and existence of a real representation).

For each e∈𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼𝖱𝖾𝖺𝖽𝗒e\in\mathsf{EvalSpecReady}, the datum 𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖡𝖺𝗌𝖾⁢[e]\mathsf{EvalTimeBase}[e] is uniquely determined, and <e<_{e} is a strict linear order on QeQ_{e}. Moreover,

Ω[e]:={ρ:Qe→ℝ∣∀q,r∈Qe,q<er⟺ρ(q)<ρ(r)}\Omega[e]:=\{\rho:Q_{e}\to\mathbb{R}\mid\forall q\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak r% \in Q_{e}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\ q<_{e}r\Longleftrightarrow\rho(q)<\rho% (r)\}

is nonempty.

Proof.

For the single-object branch, use dynamical-description operability and Definition 5.56, Definition 5.65, and Definition 5.59. For the joint branch, the same source set, order and generated equivalence relation determine the same canonical time quotient, natural projection, generating edges and reflexive transitive closure. The antisymmetry and incomparability-transitivity conditions contained in each object’s dynamical-description operability therefore give the same order-time quotient and strict linear order. Each individual trajectory domain is a subset of this common quotient, and their intersection is unique. Since the object set is nonempty, a real order embedding for one object gives an embedding of the common quotient. Agreement of the quotient and order makes this existence condition independent of the object used. ∎

Proof.

By Definition 5.90, at least one output value corresponds to each element of the relation domain. Right uniqueness in Definition 5.89 makes that output value unique. Hence there exists a map taking each domain element to its unique corresponding output value, and its graph equals the law-candidate relation. A map with the same graph takes the same value at every domain element and is therefore unique. ∎

The graph 𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽𝖣𝖠𝖦\mathsf{LawCondDAG} is a directed acyclic graph. Its root-node set is {1,2,4}\{1\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 2\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 4\}, and the strict-ancestor sets of its nodes are

Anc⁡(1)=Anc⁡(2)=Anc⁡(4)=∅,Anc⁡(3)={1},Anc⁡(5)={1,3}.\begin{gathered}\operatorname{Anc}(1)=\operatorname{Anc}(2)=\operatorname{Anc}% (4)=\varnothing\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\\ \operatorname{Anc}(3)=\{1\}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad\operatorname{% Anc}(5)=\{1\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 3\}.\end{gathered}

For every (i,j)∈𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽𝖤𝖽𝗀𝖾𝖲𝖾𝗍(i\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak j)\in\mathsf{LawCondEdgeSet}, one has 𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽𝖱𝖺𝗇𝗄⁢(i)<𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽𝖱𝖺𝗇𝗄⁢(j)\mathsf{LawCondRank}(i)<\mathsf{LawCondRank}(j) ; hence no directed cycle exists. Expanding the edge set gives the root-node set and strict-ancestor sets. ∎

Proposition 5.104 (Typing and five-condition preservation under law-datum transport).

Under the preceding definition,

𝖣′:=𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖳𝗋𝖺𝗇𝗌𝗉𝗈𝗋𝗍⁢[𝖣;τ]∈𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖣𝖺𝗍𝖲𝗉.\mathsf{D}^{\prime}:=\mathsf{LawTimeTransport}[\mathsf{D};\tau]\in\mathsf{% LawEvalDatSp}.

Moreover, the five law conditions and the common valid-time domain satisfy

∀i∈𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽𝖭𝗈𝖽𝖾𝖲𝖾𝗍,𝐊ilaw⁢[𝖣′]⟺𝐊ilaw⁢[𝖣],\forall i\in\mathsf{LawCondNodeSet}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad\mathbf{% K}^{\mathrm{law}}_{i}[\mathsf{D}^{\prime}]\Longleftrightarrow\mathbf{K}^{% \mathrm{law}}_{i}[\mathsf{D}]\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak
𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗆𝗈𝗇𝖵𝖺𝗅𝗂𝖽𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖣𝗈𝗆law⁢[𝖣′]=τ⁢[𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗆𝗈𝗇𝖵𝖺𝗅𝗂𝖽𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖣𝗈𝗆law⁢[𝖣]].\mathsf{CommonValidTimeDom}^{\mathrm{law}}[\mathsf{D}^{\prime}]=\tau\!\left[% \mathsf{CommonValidTimeDom}^{\mathrm{law}}[\mathsf{D}]\right].
Proof.

Images under the bijection and restrictions of its inverse give the nine components the types required by Definition 5.82. The admissible domains form a family of subsets of 𝕋′\mathbb{T}^{\prime}, and each conjugated change is a bijection. Thus the transported outer datum belongs to the same law-evaluation space.

For the first condition, bijective images preserve nonemptiness and membership in the applicability domain. For the second condition, replacing the time component by a bijection while retaining the input and output values preserves and reflects right uniqueness of the output. For the third condition, evaluation tuples are transported by τaeval\tau_{a}^{\mathrm{eval}}, which preserves and reflects membership in the candidate relation. For the fourth condition, the definitions of the relation image and conjugated changes make image invariance equivalent before and after transport. Each individual valid-time domain is the image of its original domain under τ\tau. Since bijective images commute with intersections, the displayed equality of common valid-time domains follows. Nonemptiness and membership in the admissible-domain family are also preserved, giving equivalence of the fifth condition. ∎

Substitution into the definition of the side-specific local numerical curve gives the side-specific equality. The definitions of the local numerical value curve and the value-coordinate chart give the value-coordinate equality. ∎

Definition 5.120 (Common evaluation rule for the differential conditions).

The five conditions below are predicates on the typed differential-evaluation structures of this section. An input to the fifth condition is a pair of structures belonging to the same base law datum and sharing the components specified in that definition. Let DD be the subset of inputs on which all assumptions in a condition’s definition hold, and let PP be its test on that domain. Define the condition by

K⁢[x]⟺∃y∈D,x=y∧P⁢[y].K[x]\Longleftrightarrow\exists y\in D\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\quad x=y\ % \wedge\ P[y].

The test displayed in each definition is its restriction to DD. The domain of the third condition is the truth domain of the second; that of the fourth is the truth domain of the first; and that of the fifth requires the first condition for both structures. In the first and second conditions, requirements that type subsequent expressions, such as openness and differentiability, are tested first. If a required type or preceding condition is absent, the condition is false; jets and change maps are not evaluated outside their domains.

hold.

For every

θ∈𝖢𝗁𝖺𝗋𝗍𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖣𝗈𝗆^a;χ0diff,\theta\in\widehat{\mathsf{ChartEvalTimeDom}}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a;\chi_{0}}% \mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak
𝖦𝖾𝗇𝖾𝗋𝖺𝗍𝖾𝖽𝖳𝗋𝗃𝖩𝖾𝗍a;χ0diff,(ka)⁢(θ)∈𝖩𝖾𝗍𝖱𝖾𝗅a;χ0diff.\mathsf{GeneratedTrjJet}^{\mathrm{diff}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak(k_{a})}_{% a;\chi_{0}}(\theta)\in\mathsf{JetRel}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a;\chi_{0}}.
Proof.

By the differential-atlas regularity condition, the time-chart-change and value-chart-change maps are bijections of class

Cka,C^{k_{a}}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak

and the reverse chart-change maps are also of class

Cka.C^{k_{a}}.

The

rr

th derivative after a value-chart change, for

0≤r≤ka,0\leq r\leq k_{a}\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak

is determined by the chain rule from the derivatives through order

rr

of the value-chart-change map and the representative curve germ. The

rr

th derivative after a time-chart change is determined by the chain rule from the derivatives through order

rr

of the inverse time-chart-change map and the representative curve germ. Hence the values of the two jet-change maps are independent of the choice of representative curve germ.

Every element of a jet-change domain can be represented by restricting a local polynomial curve through its zeroth-order component to a sufficiently small neighborhood, as the jet of a value-curve germ of class

CkaC^{k_{a}}

of order

ka.k_{a}.

Hence the two jet-change maps are defined over their entire respective jet-change domains. Two maps satisfying the same representative formula agree at every jet, so uniqueness holds.

A chart change from a chart to itself is the identity map, which gives the two identity formulas. On triple overlaps, the value-chart-change maps satisfy the value-chart composition condition, and the time-chart-change maps satisfy the time-chart composition condition. Applying two jet-change maps to a representative curve germ and using the uniqueness of each jet-change map gives the two composition formulas.

By the membership formula in Definition  5.122 , each generated trajectory jet is an element of the local jet space indexed by the same law index, time-chart reference, and value-chart reference. By the membership formula in Definition  5.123 , each generated trajectory jet belongs to the local jet relation indexed by the same law index, time-chart reference, and value-chart reference. ∎

Lemma 5.125 (Transport of a relation restriction by a bijection).

Suppose that a bijection

F:X⟶YF:X\longrightarrow Y

and subsets

A⊆X,B⊆YA\subseteq X\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad B\subseteq Y

satisfy

∀x∈X,x∈A⟺F⁢(x)∈B.\forall x\in X\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak\qquad x\in A\Longleftrightarrow F(% x)\in B.

Then

F⁢(A)=BF(A)=B

holds.

Proof.

Let y∈F⁢(A)y\in F(A). There exists x∈A⊆Xx\in A\subseteq X such that y=F⁢(x)y=F(x). Since the assumption gives F⁢(x)∈BF(x)\in B, one has y∈By\in B. Conversely, let y∈By\in B. Surjectivity gives y=F⁢(x)y=F(x) for some x∈Xx\in X, and the assumption then gives x∈Ax\in A. Hence y∈F⁢(A)y\in F(A). The two inclusions give the equality. ∎

Proposition 5.134 (Separation of order covariance from the two kinds of jet-relation covariance).

The map

𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖨𝗆𝗀𝖨𝗌𝗈o;0→1\mathsf{TimeImgIso}_{o;0\to 1}

determined by two real-valued time-order embeddings is a strictly monotone order isomorphism. Value-jet-relation covariance is given by 𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽4univ\mathsf{DiffCond}^{\mathrm{univ}}_{4}, and the image-set equality of Proposition  5.127 holds for the value-jet-change maps that preserve the time-chart index. Time-representation-change jet-relation covariance is given by 𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽5univ\mathsf{DiffCond}^{\mathrm{univ}}_{5}, and the image-set equality of Proposition  5.129 holds for the time-jet-change maps that preserve the value-chart index.

Proof.

The order isomorphism between the images follows from Proposition  5.129 . Value-jet-relation covariance follows from Definition  5.126 and Proposition  5.127 . Time-representation-change jet-relation covariance follows from Definition  5.128 and Proposition  5.129 . A value-jet change preserves the time-chart index, whereas a time-jet change preserves the value-chart index. The order isomorphism between the images assumes neither jet-relation covariance condition. The conditions establishing the three conclusions are therefore distinct. ∎

The first equality preserves the time-chart index, and the second preserves the value-chart index.

Proof.

Differential-stage operability gives the five universal differential conditions. By Proposition  5.129 , the map between the images is a strictly monotone order isomorphism. The displayed composition identity follows from Definition  5.128 .

Take a map ψ\psi satisfying the same composition identity. The map ρo,0\rho_{o\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0} is surjective onto its image, and both maps, after precomposition with ρo,0\rho_{o\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 0}, agree with ρo,1\rho_{o\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak 1}. Lemma  4.181 therefore gives ψ=𝖳𝗂𝗆𝖾𝖨𝗆𝗀𝖨𝗌𝗈o;0→1\psi=\mathsf{TimeImgIso}_{o;0\to 1}.

The value-jet-relation image-set equality follows from 𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽4univ\mathsf{DiffCond}^{\mathrm{univ}}_{4} and Proposition  5.127 . The time-jet-relation image-set equality follows from 𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖢𝗈𝗇𝖽5univ\mathsf{DiffCond}^{\mathrm{univ}}_{5} and Proposition  5.129 . ∎

5.5 Three-layer synthesis of dynamical, law-bearing, and differential descriptions

Dynamical-description operability, law-description operability, and differential-stage operability have a cumulative dependency relation.

Theorem 5.138 (Three-layer synthesis theorem for dynamical, law-bearing, and differential descriptions).

For the single-object specification 𝖤𝗏\mathsf{Ev}, use the constructed base law datum 𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖣𝖺𝗍\mathsf{LawEvalDat}, together with its base representation ρ0\rho^{0}. For the differential stage, fix a differential-evaluation-structure family belonging to this same pair. Thus 𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖣𝖺𝗍.𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖲𝗉𝖾𝖼=ιsingle⁢(𝖤𝗏)\mathsf{LawEvalDat}.\mathsf{EvalSpec}=\iota_{\mathrm{single}}(\mathsf{Ev}) . Consequently,

𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝗍𝗂𝗏𝖾⁢[𝖣𝗂𝖿𝖿𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖣𝖺𝗍]\displaystyle\mathsf{DiffOperative}[\mathsf{DiffEvalDat}] ⟹𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝗍𝗂𝗏𝖾⁢[𝖫𝖺𝗐𝖤𝗏𝖺𝗅𝖣𝖺𝗍]\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\mathsf{LawOperative}[\mathsf{LawEvalDat}]
⟹𝖣𝗒𝗇𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝗍𝗂𝗏𝖾⁢[𝖤𝗏]\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\mathsf{DynOperative}[\mathsf{Ev}]
⟹𝖤𝗑𝖺𝖼𝗍𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝖻𝗅𝖾⁢[𝖨].\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ExactOperable}[\mathsf{I}].

Under dynamical-description operability, the set of real-valued time-order embeddings is nonempty, and the dynamical-description object and dynamical-description witness object relative to each embedding exist uniquely. Under law-description operability, the observer-time law core relative to each embedding exists uniquely, and generated representability of law-evaluation time holds. Under differential-stage operability, for every

ρo∈𝖮𝗋𝖽𝖤𝗆𝖻𝖲𝖾𝗍o⁢(ℝ),\rho_{o}\in\mathsf{OrdEmbSet}_{o}(\mathbb{R})\mathchar 44\relax\allowbreak

are determined. The dynamical-description object, dynamical-description witness object, and observer-time law core exist uniquely; moreover, the order isomorphism between time-representation embedding images, value-jet-relation covariance, and time-representation-change jet-relation covariance hold.

Proof.

The first equivalence follows from Definition 5.70, the second from Definition 5.102, and the third from Definition 5.132. The first step of the implication chain follows from Definition 5.132, the second from Definition 5.102 and Proposition 5.86, and the third from Definition 5.70.

Existence and uniqueness of the dynamical-description object and dynamical-description witness object follow from Theorem 5.112; existence and uniqueness of the observer-time law core and generated representability of law-evaluation time follow from Theorem 5.113. Differential-stage operability gives the five universal differential conditions. The chart-compatible differential law and the differential-failure evaluation input are determined by Definition 5.133 and Definition 5.136, respectively. The three covariance conclusions follow from Theorem 5.135. ∎

Lemma 5.146 (Common construction of the joint-time quotients).

Assume 𝖤𝗑𝖺𝖼𝗍𝖮𝗉𝖾𝗋𝖺𝖻𝗅𝖾⁢[𝖨]\mathsf{ExactOperable}[\mathsf{I}]. Under KJointCTime⁢(𝖤𝗏)K_{\mathrm{JointCTime}}(\mathsf{Ev}), the canonical time quotients, natural projections and generated time preorders agree across all objects. If

KGenTimeOrdAntiSym⁢(𝖤𝗏ζ),KObsTimeIncTrans⁢(𝖤𝗏ζ)K_{\mathrm{GenTimeOrdAntiSym}}(\mathsf{Ev}_{\zeta})\mathchar 44\relax% \allowbreak\qquad K_{\mathrm{ObsTimeIncTrans}}(\mathsf{Ev}_{\zeta})

hold for every object, the order-time quotients, order-time projections and strict linear orders also agree. The object index may therefore be omitted from these common time objects. Agreement of the individual state quotients or individual trajectory domains is not required.

Proof.

The same equivalence relation on the same set defines the same quotient and natural projection. The same source order is mapped by the same projection, so the generating edges and their reflexive transitive closures agree. Under the antisymmetry condition, the canonical time partial orders agree, as do their strict parts, incomparability relations and quotients by incomparability. The definitions of the order-time projection and strict linear order give the conclusion. ∎
